newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico's 1.33 pct CPI seen positive.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Mexico's 1.33 pct CPI seen positive.

text.p: A 1.33 percent rise in Mexico's consumer price index in August was better than the market expected and should spell further Cetes rates declines, analysts said on Monday.

"What we're seeing is that inflation continues to come down. That's good," said John Welch of Lehman Brothers in New York. "It allows (the government) more leeway in bringing rates down," he said, adding, however that "it's hard to bring them down much further."
A consensus of analysts forecasts in a Reuters survey put the August CPI rise at 1.36 percent. On Friday, Trade Minister Herminio Blanco said it would be 1.3 percent.

Analysts said Blanco's forecast may have helped Mexico's Cetes and peso markets on Monday, but they did not expect the official figure to disappoint, even though it showed the trade minister was overly optimistic.

"The data are good," economist Carlo Ortiz said. "The market was expecting something like 1.36 percent and this number was good enough that inflation should come in at 26 or 27 percent at the end of the year."

He noted however that a continued strong inflation performance was linked to tight control of the monetary base. Lehman's Welch described monetary policy as "a tad too loose", but he said the danger was offset by the lingering heavy demand for pesos.
Gray Newman, economist at HSBC James Capel, noted that this was the best monthly inflation performance since the December 1994 peso devaluation, but he said it was largely factored in by the markets.
"August is usually the best month in terms of seaonal variations...but people are focusing on the end of the year."

He said inflation will rise at a faster clip in September as school costs filter through. Inflation in the last quarter will depend on when the government signs a wage-price alliance with business and labor, he added.
